main_text.p: rat atque confirmat: vsque ad v. 8. Deinde for-mam interitus mundi graphicè describit.
main_text.head: SVMMÆ CAPITVM.
Cap. I.
main_text.p: Omnia per Christum supremi rectoris olympi Tradidit, illius nec dubitata fides. Hancque probant sancti, simul hac pater ipse probauit, Cuncta igitur fidei nomine ferre decet.
2Nec frustra hac moneo: doctores nempe futuros Aspicio falsos, qui mala multa ferant. Qui fastu turgent, queis cordi est sola voluptas, Sed perdet fortis pectore falsa Deus.
3Condatis memori, quæ dixi pectore verba: Nam patient homines vltima secla malos, Vltima qui sperant venturæ tempora lucis, Sed vobis veræ sit pietatis amor.
main_text.head: BREVIVS.
Cap. I.
main_text.p: Admonet ista Petrus morti vicinus, amicos, Quam sit certa fides, scriptaque voxque probant.
2Blasphemos terret, immorans Loth, Noa, Gomorrham, Illos qui redeunt si fuge canisque nonant.
3Christe licet tarde, venient elementa liquescent, Expectate diem, Paulus vt ille iubet.
main_text.head: Breuissimè.
Declaratio.

p.i: Lucifer donec oriatur in cordibus vestris. v. 19. vtque Volutabris sus tota voluitur: v. 22. Elementa liquescent in fine mundi. v. 10.

page.notes: Superscript numbers 1, 2, 3 stand above "Lucifer", "vtque" and "Elementa" in the Breuissimè line; they are reference marks and are not transcribed as text. Doubtful readings: "probante"/"probant", "Condatis", "patient", "fortis", "nonant" and "fuge" are uncertain and should be checked against the scan. The line "Blasphemos terret, immorans" has a damaged initial letter, read as "m". The facing page is only a strip at the right edge and is not transcribed. The page number is at the head left, printed as "330".
